previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of bioprosthetic aortic valve, pacemaker, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, and chronic pain presented with dyspnea, weakness, and nausea. She had recently lost 21 pounds, initially attributed to overdiuresis from torsemide. Labs showed acute kidney injury with elevated BUN and creatinine, and normal cardiac enzymes and proBNP. Chest X-ray revealed no acute process. The torsemide was held, and she improved subjectively. She was transitioned to furosemide 40 mg daily and discharged home with instructions to follow up closely with her heart failure team, monitor daily weights, and avoid restarting torsemide without guidance. Her symptoms stabilized, and she was ambulatory with a walker at discharge.
